senses.gloss: (British) A small vehicle used to carry a load and pulled or pushed by hand.
A small, one-wheeled (or rarely, two-wheeled) cart with handles at one end for transporting small loads.
A small cart, normally with two or four wheels, that can be pushed by hand.
A cart designed to be pulled or pushed by hand (as opposed to with a beast of burden.)
(figurative) A critical point marking a change in course or development.
A decision point; a turning point or opportunity to change a direction, a course, or a goal.
A medical doctor specializing in the eye: deficiencies of vision requiring correction, and diseases. Compare optometrist.
A sports facility specialized for lifting weights, cardio machines, and other exercise (culturally differentiated from sense 1).
place for indoor sports — see also gym
Permitted, authorized. [from 16th c.]
large advertisement along side of highway

A large cylindrical tank used for storing gas, especially town gas (1870s-1940s) or natural gas (1950s-present). Types include one with telescopic sections with wet seals in between and one with a nontelescoping tank and a dry seal.
A ridge or hill of ice in an ice field.
sequence of letters and numbers added to a postal address
A paste, normally used with a toothbrush, for cleaning the teeth.
Toothpaste or any other substance, such as powder, for cleaning the teeth.
The act of exporting.
The state of being banished from one's home or country.
The act of banishing.
A convenient collection, in a form resembling a book, of small paper items for individual use.
A book specially designed to keep photographs, stamps, or autographs.
A process by which a task is completed; a way of doing something (followed by the adposition of, to or for before the purpose of the process).
To make a threat against someone; to use threats.
To menace or intimidate.
Initialism of personal computer.
(idiomatic) Practical; realistic; pragmatic.
One who is in charge or something.
The head cook of a restaurant or other establishment.
A person who conducts an orchestra, choir or other music ensemble; a professional whose occupation is conducting.
(music) The conductor of a musical ensemble, especially a brass or military band.
Something secret or unexplainable; an unknown.

An atmospheric phenomenon created by charged particles from the sun striking the upper atmosphere, creating coloured lights in the sky. It is usually named australis or borealis based on whether it is in the Southern or Northern Hemisphere respectively.
To survey, look at something in a wide angle.
Having prejudices.
Exhibiting prejudice or bias.
A large river in Africa flowing through Khartoum and Cairo into the Mediterranean Sea, usually considered to be the longest river in the world.

Either of two species of fast-running bird in the genus Geococcyx of the cuckoo family native to North and Central America, the lesser roadrunner (Geococcyx velox) and, especially, the greater roadrunner (Geococcyx californianus).
The key on a typewriter that moves the head one position backwards.
Malware that holds the data of a computer user for ransom, usually requiring or claiming to require payment to restore access.
An artist who primarily makes drawings.
A snack food made from corn or maize kernels popped by dry heating.
Incapable of producing results, useless; doomed not to be successful; not worth attempting.
Any of several species of fish in Salmonidae, closely related to salmon, and distinguished by spawning more than once.
Enjoyed by a small, loyal group.
protective head covering
A helmet.
(by extension) A member of any Finnic nationality, such as (more narrowly) a Baltic Finn such as a Karelian or Estonian, or (more broadly) a Volga Finn or Perm Finn.
Of or pertaining to Finland or the Finns; Finlandic, Finlandish.
The area covered by a mobile phone (cellphone) or other radio network.
(usually, in the plural) Land that is covered mostly with water, with occasional marshy and soggy areas.
Irritating, stressful or bothersome.
Imposing or constituting a physical, mental, or figurative load which can be borne only with effort; burdensome.
(North America, by extension) Involving hard work and struggle.
An island in the Mediterranean, and the largest in Greece.
Product; the result of effort.
The manner of spelling of words; correct spelling.
Correct spelling according to established usage; also (obsolete) pronunciation according to the spelling of a word.
(Greek god) The Greek god of war, considered equivalent to the Roman Mars and usually described as a son of Zeus and Hera, companion of Eris and Enyo, and by Aphrodite father of Deimos and Phobos.
Place or position.
The residential area near one's home.
Proximity; the state of being near.
The area surrounding someone or something, together with the objects and circumstances in the vicinity; the environment or ambiance.
The outside boundary, parts or surface of something.
(biology) organism that exists by stealing resources from another organism
Of or pertaining to a biological or symbolic parasite.
(pejorative) A lazy or irresponsible person who is often unemployed, often depending upon wealthy or otherwise financially independent people for support.
Someone who looks after the maintenance and cleaning of a public building.
An inclination in a particular direction.
An exercise done to improve upper body strength, performed by resting on one's toes and hands and pushing one's weight off the floor.
(uncountable) Alluring beauty or charm (often with sex appeal).
(uncountable) The property of being lovely, of attractiveness, beauty, appearing to be lovable.
tree of the genus Carpinus
The state of being graceful.
Having the aroma or flavor of lime.
(legal) A contract which binds a person to work for another, under specified conditions, for a specified time (often as an apprentice).
Someone who sleeps.
A sleepy person.
Superfluous; exceeding what is necessary, no longer needed.
The act of corroding or the condition so produced.
To obstruct the passage of (someone or something).
To disallow; to proscribe.
(transitive) To forbid, disallow, or proscribe officially; to make illegal or illicit.
To exclude or shut out; to bar.
Very large.
Operated by, performed by, or transporting a person; crewed; piloted; staffed.
pertaining to space
To determine and declare (property) to be assigned to public use. See eminent domain.

A device used for performing arithmetical calculations; (rare) a table on which loose counters are placed, or (more commonly) an instrument with beads sliding on rods, or counters in grooves, with one row of beads or counters representing units, the next tens, etc.
An artificial passage for water, fitted with a valve or gate, for example in a canal lock or a mill stream, for stopping or regulating the flow.
A board, usually square, covered with such a pattern; especially such a board with 8×8 squares, used to play chess and draughts/checkers.

(mathematics) A diagram in which the relationship between three variables is represented by a straight line or curve for each variable; the value of the third variable corresponding to particular values of the first two is obtained by drawing a straight line through the points on the first two curves that represent particular values of the first two variables and noting the point at which the line intersects the third line or curve.
A mild expression of surprise or enthusiasm.
(transitive, grammar) To build (a sentence, an argument, etc.) by arranging words or ideas.
To make something by merging parts.
The state or condition of being infectious.
The state or condition of being contagious.
The state of being clueless.
An instance of wallowing.
A groove, deep furrow, elongated cleft or tear between body parts or in the substance of an organ.
A performer of tricks or an escapologist or an illusionist.
(photography) Of or relating to a technique in which exposures are taken at fewer intervals than usual so that, on playback, a naturally slow process may be viewed at an accelerated pace.

A synthetic, crystalline compound, C₆H₇N₃O, (trademarks Hydra, Hyzyd, Isovit, Laniazid, Nydrazid, Rimifon, Stanozide) used as a bacteriostatic medication in the prevention and treatment of tuberculosis.
The largest city in Pakistan situated along the Arabian Sea, as well as the provincial capital of Sindh Province.
Exercise with the goal of raising the heart rate by walking or running on the treadmill.
A vehicle with skis at the front and a caterpillar track at the rear, used for travelling over snow, sometimes as sport.
A positively charged ion: one that would be attracted to the cathode in electrolysis.
A cloth or stuff made of matted fibres of wool, or wool and fur, fulled or wrought into a compact substance by rolling and pressure, with lees or size, without spinning or weaving.
The dried leaf of one of these plants, the South American shrub (Erythroxylum coca), widely cultivated in Andean countries, which is the source of cocaine and used as aphrodisiac in the past.
One who composes; an author.
A condition of severely stunted physical and mental growth due to the untreated congenital deficiency of thyroid hormones.
Someone who calls for the seizure or recovery of territories or states currently subject to other countries; an adherent of irredentism.
A high-pitched, silly laugh.
A joyful, somewhat muffled laugh, rather like a snorting chuckle.
(intransitive) To move; to be shifted from a fixed position.

A fretted stringed instrument, similar to the guitar, having a bowl-shaped body or soundbox; any of a wide variety of chordophones with a pear-shaped body and a neck whose upper surface is in the same plane as the soundboard, with strings along the neck and parallel to the soundboard.
Any of many symbiotic organisms, being associations of algae and fungi, often found as white or yellow-to-blue–green patches on rocks, old walls, etc.
A en given name.

A treatment, typically using ultrasound shock waves or crushing with a surgical instrument, by which a kidney stone or similar calculus is broken into particles small enough to be voided or washed out.
obstacle
A town and municipality on Lake Geneva in Riviera-Pays-d'Enhaut district, Vaud Canton, Switzerland.
person who organizes and operates a business and assumes the associated risk
To carry or bear from one place to another; to remove; to convey.
To adopt a word from another language.
(transitive) To carry or transport something, with a connotation that the item is heavy or otherwise difficult to move.
The belief in unification of the peoples and countries of the Arab World.
(enzyme) A digestive enzyme that chemically digests, or breaks down, proteins into shorter chains of amino acids.
A traditional French Provençal stewed vegetable dish consisting primarily of tomatoes, zucchini and eggplant.
The branch of medicine specializing in arthritis and other ailments of the joints.
To become aware of the loss or absence of; to feel the want or need of, sometimes with regret; to feel sadness at the absence of somebody or something.
(neurology, psychology) A neurological or psychological phenomenon whereby a particular sensory stimulus triggers a second kind of sensation. [from late 19th c.]

Someone skilled in the writing of shorthand or the use of a stenotype machine, especially for the purpose of rapid transcription of speech. One employed in such a role: a professional transcriptionist who employs shorthand.
A gradual diminishing of strength.
The achievement of one's aim or goal.
Excessive work.
To cease to subscribe to (a feed of another user's activity).
A tribute given in appreciation of someone's service etc.

One of the six federal states of Australia, consisting of one large, eponymous and several much smaller islands, off the eastern part of Australia's south coast; a former British colony, from 1856 to 1901. Capital: Hobart.

To cause to be ashamed; to abash.
To make ashamed; to embarrass; to destroy the self-possession of, as by exciting suddenly a consciousness of guilt, mistake, or inferiority; to disconcert; to discomfit.
A person who walks about in their sleep; a sleepwalker.
A dry, or sweet apéritif wine flavored with aromatic herbs, and often used in mixed drinks.
belief
Motion across a body of water in a craft powered by the wind, as a sport or otherwise
(nautical) Skill in, and knowledge of, the work of navigating, maintaining, and operating a vessel at sea.
